# name: ra-wallis-monotone-test
# technique: test a claim no recipe certifies, at instances Sage evaluates exactly or by intervals
# goal: sage_test KaluzaKlein.RealAnalysis.Exercises.wallis_monotone file "ra-wallis-monotone-test.sage"
# description: Sage's exact I_(2n+1) ≤ I_(2n) ≤ I_(2n-1)
SEED = 0  # the instances are listed, no sampling
R = RealIntervalField(128)
def B(b):
    return QQ(1 if bool(b) else 0)
RI = RealIntervalField(256)
def O(values, lhs, rhs, rel='==', edge=False):
    # symbolic values (π, e, logs, limits Sage computed) are compared by 256-bit intervals; rationals exactly
    if any(hasattr(v, 'parent') and v.parent() is SR for v in (lhs, rhs)):
        lhs, rhs = RI(lhs), RI(rhs)
    return oracle_instance(*values, lhs=lhs, rhs=rhs, relation=rel, edge=edge)
x = var('x')
I_ = lambda m: integrate(sin(x) ** m, x, 0, pi / 2)
instances = [O([str(n), '(by norm_num)'], B(RI(I_(2 * n + 1)) <= RI(I_(2 * n)) and RI(I_(2 * n)) <= RI(I_(2 * n - 1))), QQ(1), edge=bool(n == 1)) for n in [1, 2, 5]]
